title: HIV, ART timing, and TB
dek: Start ART within two weeks of TB therapy for most people with HIV, regardless of CD4. Meningitis is the exception: wait 4–8 weeks. Rifamycin induction is the other clock.
story: WHO: ART should start as soon as possible within two weeks of DS-TB treatment initiation, regardless of CD4, in people without meningitis. The old “wait until CD4 > x” delay killed people with advanced HIV. For DR-TB, ART within eight weeks is the written strong recommendation; many clinicians still aim earlier when the CNS is quiet.

TB meningitis (and cryptococcal meningitis) is the IRIS exception: earlier ART increased adverse events without a mortality win. Delay ART at least 4 weeks and start by 8 weeks, with steroids on board for TBM.

Rifampin induces UGT/CYP and halves dolutegravir exposure unless DTG is given twice daily. Protease inhibitors and rifampin are a mess; rifabutin overlays exist in CDC-land. Rifapentine still induces. Bedaquiline is CYP3A4-sensitive — rifamycins and BDQ are not co-travelers in BPaLM (you already dropped RIF).
deepTitle: IRIS is immunology, not failure of the TB drugs
deep: Paradoxical IRIS: known TB, worsening after ART. Unmasking IRIS: occult TB appears after ART. Steroids for severe TBM-IRIS; do not automatically switch to MDR therapy because a lymph node grew.
Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis remains part of advanced HIV care alongside TB therapy.
LF-LAM plus mWRD before ART in advanced HIV is how you avoid unmasking surprises — screen, don’t just start.
CD4 20 vs 400 no longer changes the two-week pulmonary ART rule; it still changes diagnostic yield and IRIS risk.

visual.caption: ART clocks: two weeks for pulmonary/disseminated TB; 4–8 weeks for TBM. Rifamycin–DTG twice-daily is the pharmacologic patch, not a reason to withhold ART.

example.title: CD4 18, pulmonary TB, DTG once daily + RIF
example.setup: New DS-TB, HIV newly diagnosed, CD4 18, started 2HRZE, DTG/3TC/TDF once daily.

steps.title: ART timing is already right-ish
steps.body: Start ART now, not after a month of watching CD4. No meningitis.

steps.title: DTG must be BID with rifampin
steps.body: Once-daily DTG is under-dosed on RIF. This is a chart error, not a “wait and see.”

steps.title: Watch IRIS, do not stop RIF for it by default
steps.body: Fever and node enlargement at week 3 of ART can be IRIS. Culture/NAAT to exclude a second pathogen or missed RR.

example.takeaway: Two-week ART plus a rifamycin–ART patch. Meningitis is the only routine delay.

check.prompt: For pulmonary TB in a person with HIV and no meningitis, WHO says start ART:
choices: As soon as possible within two weeks of TB treatment, regardless of CD4
check.answer: As soon as possible within two weeks of TB treatment, regardless of CD4
check.why: The CD4-stratified delay is outdated for pulmonary TB.

check.prompt: HIV-associated TBM: ART should be delayed:
choices: At least 4 weeks, initiated by 8 weeks, with adjunctive steroids
check.answer: At least 4 weeks, initiated by 8 weeks, with adjunctive steroids
check.why: IRIS in a closed skull is the reason.

check.prompt: On the ART-timing map, DTG BID is attached to which path?
choices: The early ART path when rifampin is used
check.answer: The early ART path when rifampin is used
check.why: Induction patch, not a meningitis patch.
